alignments.note: γάρ → *For*.
πᾶς → *every*, standing before an expressed noun rather than a substantival article, so rule 80 is not in question.
Rule 66 names ἀρχιερεύς → *high priest* headed on *priest*.
Passive καθίσταται → *is appointed*, headed on the lexical participle under rule 9.
Rule 61: the preposition governing an articular infinitive takes the English clause-introducer, here the bare infinitival *to*.
Nominalizing article of the articular infinitive; rule 61 with rule 23.
προσφέρειν → *offer*, the marker having gone to εἰς.
τε → *both*.
δῶρα → *gifts*; the ASV reorders relative to the Greek, which rule 15 permits.
καί → *and*.
θυσίας → *sacrifices*.
ὅθεν → *wherefore*.
Verbless clause with no expressed subject: rule 68 puts the supplied subject and copula on the predicate adjective, headed on *necessary*.
Rule 85: the supplied complementizer belongs to the non-finite complement the ASV expands into a finite clause, so *that … have* is one discontinuous unit under rule 15, headed on the verb.

Substantival demonstrative τοῦτον → *this*. The demonstrative keeps only its own English word: the italicized *high priest* that follows is not the kind of generic completion rules 17 and 49 fold onto a demonstrative but a full lexical repetition of ἀρχιερεύς, already spent at t003–t004, so rule 103 makes it its own `added` unit.

Rule 103: supplied English lexical content whose source token is already realized elsewhere in the verse is `added`, and rule 7 does not fold it. ἀρχιερεύς (s003) is spent on *high priest* at t003–t004, and a full lexical noun is not among rule 7's helpers, so the repetition answers to no available token. Headed on *priest* under rule 66. Reading it as a discontinuous second realization of s003 under rule 15, or as a rule 49-style completion of the demonstrative, remains defensible; I took `added` because the supplied noun is a resumed head noun rather than a generic *one* or *thing*, which is the only expansion rules 17 and 49 fold onto a demonstrative.
Intensifying καί → *also* under rule 65's English-side test.
Indefinite τι → *somewhat*.

The relative clause ὃ προσενέγκῃ is rendered by an English infinitive, so under rule 40's principle the relative is realized by the word introducing its English clause, the infinitival *to*. Reading *to* as the infinitive's own rule 7 marker and leaving ὅ `unrepresented` remains defensible; I took the rule 40 analysis because a source token governs the clause.
προσενέγκῃ → *offer*.

review_notes: Corrected the τοῦτον unit: the italicized *high priest* is now its own `added` unit under rule 103, ἀρχιερεύς having already been spent on *high priest* earlier in the same verse, and the demonstrative keeps only *this*.
Two placement calls retained: the supplied *that* on ἔχειν under rule 85, and the relative ὅ on the infinitival *to* under rule 40's principle, both noted in their units.
εἰς τὸ προσφέρειν analysed under rule 61 with the article `unrepresented`.
Partition verified after the change: all 19 source ids and all 25 target ids used exactly once across 20 units.
